work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · II.

items.text: Pay him the wages agreed upon, or as appointed by the sheriff or sessions.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · II.
items.quote: all servants and labourers, except apprentices, become entitled to wages: according to their agreement

items.text: Do not assault or strike your master or dame.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · II.
items.quote: if any servant, workman, or labourer assaults his master or dame, he shall suffer one year's imprisonment

items.text: If you must correct him, do it in moderation, not with cruelty.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · II.
items.quote: may by law correct his apprentice or servant for negligence or other misbehaviour, so it be done with moderation

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 17: Of Guardian and Ward

items.text: Defend the ward against all attacks, both in law and otherwise, and assist and support him as his guardian.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Bk I, Ch 17
items.quote: for he is to defend him against all attacks as well by law as otherwise

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · Notes

items.text: Defend your child when their safety is threatened.
items.citation: Blackstone, Comm. 1.14 note c
items.quote: a parent for his child

items.text: Protect your wife's chastity with all necessary force.
items.citation: Blackstone, Comm. 1.14 note c
items.quote: a husband or father for the chastity of his wife

items.text: Safeguard your daughter's chastity as a matter of family honor.
items.citation: Blackstone, Comm. 1.14 note c
items.quote: a husband or father for the chastity of his ... daughter

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 15: Of Husband and Wife · II.

items.text: Pay her alimony out of your estate when separated from bed and board, as the judge settles, proportioned to her rank and quality.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 15, II
items.quote: the law allows alimony to the wife; which is that allowance, which is made to a woman for her support out of the husband's estate

items.text: Do not elope or live with an adulterer, or you will lose your alimony.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 15, II
items.quote: But in case of elopement, and living with an adulterer, the law allows her no alimony.

items.text: Do not marry another while your spouse lives, for a separation from bed and board does not dissolve the marriage.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 15, II
items.quote: the law will not allow it to be unloosed for any cause whatsoever, that arises after the union is made
items.conflict: Matthew 19:9 permits remarriage after divorce for sexual immorality.

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant · III.

items.text: Obey your master in matters that are honest and lawful.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.14.III
items.quote: he is only to obey his master in matters that are honest and lawful.

items.text: Stand by and defend your master, for this is part of your duty for which you receive wages.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.14.III
items.quote: it is part of his duty, for which he receives his wages, to stand by and defend his master.

items.text: Answer for the acts of your servant if done by your command, express or implied.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.14.III
items.quote: the master is answerable for the act of his servant, if done by his command, either expressly given, or implied

items.text: Answer for any damage your servant does to a stranger by negligence while actually employed in your service.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.14.III
items.quote: if a servant, by his negligence does any damage to a stranger, the master shall answer for his neglect

items.text: Answer for any member of your household who casts anything out of the house into the street, to the damage of any individual or the common nuisance.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.14.III
items.quote: A master is, lastly, chargeable if any of his family layeth or casteth any thing out of his house into the street

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 15: Of Husband and Wife · I.

items.text: Give free and willing consent to the marriage contract; do not enter it by force or fraud.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Husband and Wife I
items.quote: they must be willing to contract.

items.text: Remain faithful to your spouse; do not marry another while your spouse is living.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Husband and Wife I
items.quote: having another husband or wife living; in which case... the second marriage is to all intents and purposes void

items.text: Do not marry a close blood relative or in-law within the Levitical degrees; the farthest is uncle and niece.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Husband and Wife I
items.quote: nothing (God's law except) shall impeach any marriage, but within the Levitical degrees; the farthest of which is that between uncle and niece.

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 17: Of Guardian and Ward

items.text: Act as a temporary parent: provide for his maintenance and education, and manage his estate for his benefit.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: the power and reciprocal duty of a guardian and ward are the same, pro tempore, as that of a father and child

items.text: Honor and obey your guardian as a father while under his care.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: the power and reciprocal duty of a guardian and ward are the same, pro tempore, as that of a father and child

items.text: When he comes of age, give him an account of all you have transacted on his behalf, and answer for losses by your willful default or negligence.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: the guardian, when the ward comes of age, is bound to give him an account of all that he has transacted on his behalf, and must answer for all losses.

items.text: If you manage your minor child's estate as guardian, account to him for the profits.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: the father is by common law the guardian, and must account to his child for the profits

items.text: If your daughter under sixteen has no guardian assigned by her father, act as her guardian: provide for her maintenance, education, and estate.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: if none be so assigned, the mother shall in this case be guardian

items.text: Nurture your child until he is fourteen, as guardian for nurture.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.17
items.quote: guardians for nurture, which are, of course, the father or mother, till the infant attains the age of fourteen years

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 16: Of Parent and Child · II.

items.text: Provide for your child care, protection, maintenance, and education.
items.citation: Commentaries, I.16 II
items.quote: the care, the protection, the maintenance, and the education of the children should belong

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 15: Of Husband and Wife · I.

items.text: Get the consent of your father, or if he be not living of your mother or guardian, before marrying while under twenty-one.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries Book I Ch.15
items.quote: without the consent of the father, or, if he be not living, of the mother or guardians, shall be absolutely void.

items.text: Provide a husband for your daughter before she is twenty-five, or do not disinherit her if she falls.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries Book I Ch.15
items.quote: if a parent did not provide a husband for his daughter, by the time she arrived at the age of twenty five... he was not allowed to disinherit her.

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 14: Of Master and Servant

items.text: Serve your master faithfully for the whole term, throughout all seasons, whether there is work or not.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: the servant shall serve, and the master maintain him, throughout all the revolutions of the respective seasons

items.text: Maintain your servant throughout the term, throughout all seasons, whether there is work or not.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: the servant shall serve, and the master maintain him, throughout all the revolutions of the respective seasons

items.text: Instruct an apprentice in the trade or mystery for which he is bound.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: to serve their masters, and be maintained and instructed by them

items.text: Do not put away your servant before or at the end of his term without a quarter's warning or reasonable cause allowed by a justice.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: no master can put away his servant, or servant leave his master, either before or at the end of his term, without a quarter's warning

items.text: Do not leave your master's service before or at the end of your term without a quarter's warning or reasonable cause allowed by a justice.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: no master can put away his servant, or servant leave his master, either before or at the end of his term, without a quarter's warning

items.text: Do not withhold baptism from a servant for fear of losing his service; that practice is without foundation and without excuse.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: the infamous and unchristian practice of withholding baptism from negro servants, left they sould thereby gain their liberty, is totally without foundation, as well as without excuse.

items.text: Render to your master the same service after you become a Christian as you owed before; baptism does not dissolve your contract.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: whatever service the heathen negro owed to his English master, the same is he bound to render when a christian.

items.text: Grant your servant the same liberty before and after baptism; his faith does not alter his entitlement to liberty.
items.citation: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, Chapter 14
items.quote: the slave is entitled to the same liberty in England before, as after, baptism

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 16: Of Parent and Child · II. … Notes

items.text: Maintain your child born out of wedlock; the law charges both mother and reputed father with support.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.note 2
items.quote: by charging the mother, or the reputed father with the payment of money or other sustentation for that purpose

items.text: Do not marry your daughter, even if she is a bastard.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.note 2
items.quote: a man shall not marry his bastard sister or daughter

items.text: Do not marry your sister, even if she is a bastard.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.note 2
items.quote: a man shall not marry his bastard sister or daughter

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 16: Of Parent and Child · I.

items.text: Provide maintenance for your children; support and preserve the life you have given them.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.I
items.quote: there is an obligation on every man to provide for those descended from his loins

items.text: Protect your children as your duty.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.I
items.quote: their maintenance, their protection, and their education.

items.text: Educate your children; give them the training they need.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.I
items.quote: their maintenance, their protection, and their education.

items.text: Grandparents must maintain their poor impotent grandchildren at their own charges if able.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.I
items.quote: The father, and mother, grandfather, and grandmother of poor impotent persons shall maintain them at their own charges

items.text: A stepfather must maintain his wife's child if she had the ability to do so before their marriage.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries I.16.I
items.quote: if a mother or grandmother marries again... the husband shall be charged to maintain it

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 15: Of Husband and Wife · III.

items.text: Provide her with necessaries as much as yourself; if she contracts debts for them, pay them.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: The husband is bound to provide his wife with necessaries by law, as much as himself; and if she contracts debts for them, he is obliged to pay them.

items.text: Pay her debts contracted before marriage; you have adopted her and her circumstances together.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: If the wife be indebted before marriage, the husband is bound afterwards to pay the debt.

items.text: Concur with her in any action for injury to her person or property, and stand as defendant with her if she is sued.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: she can bring no action for redress without her husband's concurrence, and in his name, as well as her own

items.text: Do not give evidence for or against your spouse in any trial.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: they are not allowed to be evidence for, or against, each other

items.text: Do not give your wife moderate correction; though the old law allowed it, now she may have security of the peace against you, and you may restrain her liberty only for gross misbehaviour.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: The husband also (by the old law) might give his wife moderate correction.
items.conflict: Husbands must love their wives and not treat them harshly (Colossians 3:19).

items.text: Do not commit violence or threaten your spouse; either may demand security of the peace against the other.
items.citation: Blackstone, Commentaries on the Laws of England, 1.15.III
items.quote: a wife may now have security of the peace against her husband; or, in return, a husband against his wife

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 17: Of Guardian and Ward · Notes

items.text: Claim no right in the ward's inheritance; let custody remain with one from whom no such claim is suspected.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Guardian and Ward, Notes
items.quote: no one should be another's guardian, who was to enjoy the estate after his death.

items.text: Take charge of the child's education, as the mother's kin, so that guardianship and inheritance are kept distinct.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Guardian and Ward, Notes
items.quote: the education of the child to the mother's; that the guardianship and right of succession might always be kept distinct.

work: Commentaries on the Laws of England, Book I, chapters 14-17
heading: Book I, Chapter 16: Of Parent and Child · I.

items.text: Provide maintenance for your children.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: the duty of maintenance

items.text: Protect your children: maintain their lawsuits and defend their persons.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: A parent may, by our laws, maintain and uphold his children in their lawsuits, without being guilty of the legal crime of maintaining quarrels. A parent may also justify an assault and battery in defence of the persons of his children.

items.text: Give your children an education suitable to their station in life.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: a duty pointed out by reason, and of far the greatest importance of any... giving them an education suitable to their station in life.

items.text: Do not send your child beyond the seas to be instructed in the popish religion.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: if any parent, or other, shall send or convey any person beyond sea, to enter into, or be resident in, or trained up in, any priory, abbey, nunnery, popish university, college, or school... in order to be instructed, persuaded, or confirmed in the popish religion

items.text: Correct your child, being under age, in a reasonable manner, for his benefit.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: He may lawfully correct his child, being under age, in a reasonable manner ; for this is for the benefit of his education.

items.text: If you receive the profits of your child's estate during his minority, account for them to him when he comes of age.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: though he may receive the profits during the child's minority, yet he must account for them when he comes of age.

items.text: By the custom of London, leave your children at least one third of your effects, equally divided among them.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: the children of freemen are entitled to one third of their father's effects, to be equally divided among them ; of which he cannot deprive them.

items.text: Do not marry under age without your parent's consent.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: The consent or concurrence of the parent to the marriage of his child under age... without it the contract is void.

items.text: Obey your parents during your minority.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: we naturally owe subjection and obedience during our minority

items.text: Honour and reverence your parents ever after.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: honour and reverence ever after

items.text: Protect your parents in their old age, and defend their person or lawsuit if needed.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: they, who protected the weakness of our infancy, are entitled to our protection in the infirmity of their age.

items.text: Support your parents if they stand in need of assistance, even if they are wicked.
items.citation: Blackstone, Of Parent and Child I
items.quote: they who by sustenance and education have enabled their offspring to prosper, ought in return to be supported by that offspring, in case they stand in need of assistance.
